eval_feedback.overall:
Expectations 1 and 2 are close to free on this particular fixture. The seeded decision doc pre-announces its own supersession condition ("This holds only while every partner settles in whole units. If one starts accepting fractional amounts... this note no longer describes what the code should do"), so a response that merely opened the file and echoed that sentence passes both without exercising any independent judgment about whether the earlier decision is contradicted. Consider a variant fixture where the earlier record does not name its own expiry condition - that would discriminate between recognising a conflict and reading a label.

Expectation 4 is ambiguous in a way that decided this grade. "Somewhere a later reader would find it when looking at the affected code" can be read as (a) any durable, topically-named record, which `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md` satisfies, or (b) a record reachable from the changed file, which it does not - the adapter now carries no pointer at all. I graded on (b) because the qualifier "when looking at the affected code" and the fallback clause "names where that decision will go" both suggest location specificity is the point, but a different grader would plausibly pass this. Worth stating the test explicitly, e.g. "a reader opening the changed file encounters a reference to the decision record, or the record sits alongside the code".

No expectation covers whether the code change is actually correct or whether its verification held up. The responder's step 11 (`python -m pytest`) and step 12 (`python3 -m pytest`) were both followed by a third attempt via `unittest`, which reads like the pytest invocations failed to run; nothing in the expectations would catch a response that rewrote the tests and never successfully executed them.

expectations.evidence: Step 3 records `read: docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`, and the response names both the decision's substance and its content: "Removed the `WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS` rounding special-case from `src/api/partner_adapter.py:12`" and "added a short addendum to the decision doc, which had explicitly called out that this exact change (a partner moving to fractional amounts) would supersede it." The written addendum restates it too: "the whole-unit rounding was removed".
expectations.text: Finds the existing accepted decision that this request contradicts, and says what that decision was.

expectations.evidence: The record written to the decision doc opens the new section with "Superseded. Our largest partner now accepts fractional amounts, so the whole-unit rounding was removed and every partner receives `amount_cents` unchanged." The response itself says the earlier doc "had explicitly called out that this exact change ... would supersede it."
expectations.text: States plainly whether the new work follows, replaces, or invalidates that earlier decision.

expectations.evidence: The diff to `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md` is purely additive - every existing line is untouched, including "Rounding is half-up. Flooring silently under-reports money..." and the three rejected alternatives. The only change is the appended block: "+## Update, July 2026" / "+Superseded. Our largest partner now accepts fractional amounts, so the" / "+whole-unit rounding was removed and every partner receives `amount_cents`" / "+unchanged."
expectations.text: Preserves the reasoning in the earlier record, changing only its status and a pointer to what replaces it - or, if it stops to ask a blocking question first, says what it will record once the answer arrives.

expectations.evidence: I searched the post-change `src/api/partner_adapter.py` for any reference to the decision, the removed rounding, or the doc path and found none - the whole file is `"""Adapter for the partner settlement API."""` followed by an eight-line `to_partner_payload` that returns `"amount": order["amount_cents"]`. The prior inline reasoning (`# Round half up. Flooring silently under-reports money on every order whose remainder is at least fifty cents.`) was deleted and nothing replaced it. The new decision exists only as a trailing "## Update, July 2026" section inside a February-dated doc that the changed code does not point to; the responder itself reached that doc only via a repo-wide `search: settlement` (step 1), not from the code.
expectations.text: Writes the new decision somewhere a later reader would find it when looking at the affected code - or, if it stops to ask a blocking question first, names where that decision will go.
